findings.title: NPE fix is incomplete; sibling methods still dereference potentially-null model
findings.body: The PR patches only `getSubGroupsCount()` to guard against a null from `modelSupplier.get()`. The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads immediately below (lines 256, 262, 268) still do `return modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` and `getGroupModel()` itself (line 299) returns `cacheSession.getGroupDelegate().getGroupById(realm, cached.getId())` which is null when the underlying group has just been deleted concurrently. After the partial fix, those code paths will still throw NPE for exactly the scenario the PR is supposed to fix, so callers that ask for the subgroup stream (e.g. UI / admin endpoints that walk the group tree) remain broken.

findings.title: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() changes semantics and may still NPE downstream
findings.body: `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` previously either returned a count or threw. Now it silently returns `null`. The existing caller (`GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount`) forwards that to `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(group.getSubGroupsCount())`. If `setSubGroupCount` does not accept null, the NPE just moves one frame up the stack; if it does, callers of the admin REST API can now see `subGroupCount: null` where they previously got a real number. Either way this is a silent contract change that should be called out and not buried in a one-line null-check.

findings.title: Background reader thread is never joined; the assertion races the worker
findings.body: The test starts a reader thread that loops on `while (!deletedAll.get())` and stores any thrown exception in `caughtExceptions`. The Thread reference is discarded (no field, no `join()`). After `deletedAll.set(true)` the test immediately asserts `caughtExceptions.isEmpty()`. There is a real race: the reader may still be inside an in-flight `groups(...)` HTTP call when the flag flips, and the exception from that final call can be added to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated. The test should keep the Thread in a field and `join()` it before asserting.

findings.title: Test uses brief representation and may not exercise the fixed code path
findings.body: The reproducer calls `managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true)` with `briefRepresentation = true`. Brief group representations typically do not populate `subGroupCount`, so the patched `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount()` (and the NPE path) may never be reached. As written the test only proves that listing groups by `groups()` does not throw; it does not prove the actual bug from #40368 is fixed. The test should call an endpoint or method that explicitly reads the subgroup count while deletion is in progress (e.g. fetch a full representation, or invoke `getSubGroupsCount()` on the cached group).

findings.title: 100 groups are created without registering cleanup
findings.body: `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` creates up to 100 groups and stores their ids in a local list, but never calls `managedRealm.cleanup().add(...)` for any of them. If the test fails before the deletion loop completes (or before the thread is joined), all the created groups remain attached to the realm and pollute subsequent tests. Each successful `groups().add(group)` should be paired with `managedRealm.cleanup().add(r -> r.groups().group(uuid).remove())`.

findings.title: Test relies on timing; the concurrent read may complete before any delete happens
findings.body: The reader thread loops while `deletedAll` is false, but each loop iteration is a single HTTP `GET`. If the reader finishes a request just before `deletedAll` is set true, or simply iterates only a few times before the 100 deletes complete, there may be no overlap at all between read and delete and the test never exercises the concurrent path. The test would be more deterministic if it blocked deletion until the reader thread signalled that it had started, or if it performed deletes interleaved with reads inside a controlled loop rather than depending on scheduling.
